content_units: Best Meal Kit Match for a 2-Person Melbourne Household

For your priorities—  under AUD 110/week  ,   one vegetarian + one omnivore  ,   weekday cooking under 30 minutes  , and   no peanuts  —the strongest overall fit is   GreenPlate  , with   SimpleTable   as the best speed-first alternative.
Meal Kit Comparison Table
Option   Weekly Cost   Meals x Servings   Avg Cook Time   Flexibility   Likely Fit
GreenPlate     AUD 96     4 x 2     28 min     Swap allowed; 60% vegetarian menu     Best overall
HomePan     AUD 82     3 x 2     24 min     Limited swaps; mixed menu   Budget-friendly but weaker mixed-diet fit
UrbanFork     AUD 118     5 x 2     31 min     Full swaps; broad menu   Flexible, but over budget and too slow
SimpleTable     AUD 104     4 x 2     22 min     Vegetarian plan available; no cross-plan mixing   Fast, but awkward for split diets
Ranked Options
Option 1:   GreenPlate     Best balance of price, flexibility, and weeknight practicality     AUD 96 / 28 min / swap-friendly
- Stays comfortably within your   AUD 110   cap.
- Average cook time is   under 30 minutes  , so it fits weekday limits.
- The   60% vegetarian menu   plus   swap allowed   gives the best chance of building a week that works for one vegetarian and one omnivore.
- For   peanut avoidance  , this is still the option most likely to let you steer away from risky dishes through swaps.
Option 2:   SimpleTable     Best if speed matters most, but less suitable for mixed preferences     AUD 104 / 22 min / low mixing flexibility
- Excellent for busy weekdays at   22 minutes average  .
- Fits budget.

- Main drawback:   vegetarian plan available, but no cross-plan mixing  . That makes it less natural for a household where one person is vegetarian and the other is omnivore unless both are happy eating mostly vegetarian meals.
Option 3:   HomePan     Cheapest option, but fewer meals and less flexible diet matching     AUD 82 / 24 min / limited swaps
- Lowest cost and fast cooking.
- But only   3 meals/week  , so lower coverage than the 4-meal options.
-   Limited swaps   makes it harder to consistently satisfy both a vegetarian and omnivore while also avoiding peanuts.
Option 4:   UrbanFork     Most flexible menu, but misses your two biggest constraints     AUD 118 / 31 min / full swaps
- Best flexibility on paper with   full swaps   and a broad menu.
- However, it is   over budget   and   over your 30-minute weekday cap  .
- Good trade-off option only if you decide flexibility matters more than budget and speed.
Why GreenPlate Comes Out Ahead
GreenPlate best matches your priorities in order:
-   Budget:   yes, at   AUD 96
-   Weeknight time:   yes, at   28 minutes
-   Mixed diet household:   stronger fit than the others because swaps help manage vegetarian/omnivore overlap
-   Peanut avoidance:   not explicitly guaranteed from the data given, but swap flexibility improves your odds versus rigid plans
Fit Notes for Your Household
-   Best overall recommendation:     GreenPlate
-   Best if both adults are happy eating mostly vegetarian during the week:     SimpleTable
-   Best cheapest backup:     HomePan
-   Best only if constraints soften:     UrbanFork
Planning Context
I treated   “likely fit”   as a combination of:
- staying under   AUD 110/week
- meeting the   sub-30-minute weekday target
- handling a   split vegetarian/omnivore household
- reducing friction around   peanut avoidance   based on menu flexibility
Since no provider-specific allergen policy was supplied, peanut safety is judged only from the menu/swap flexibility you provided, not from a confirmed allergen-control program.
